correctness.rationale: The theorem derives the exact pair-constraint hull and full vertex list, the top-two-coordinate gauge, and active-facet strict illumination conditions. A source can illuminate at most one signed axis vertex and two sign corners. Every possible nonempty illuminated vertex pattern has strict cost larger than its cardinality (including the three-vertex pattern, in which the common corner coordinate forces gauge >3). Summing bounds gives >=\(2d+2^d\) and radial sources at (1+eps)v attain this infimum. An exact arithmetic diagnostic verifies 8,452 discrete sources but the universal argument is analytic. Boundary faces are covered because sources illuminating a vertex cross all facets containing any incident face.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The final claim is exact parameter 2^d+2d for pair-sum polars. The ordinary illumination value 6 is compatible with this result, and exact quantification for the opposite root polytope gives no general equality by duality. The \(d=4\) self-dual 24-cell case is an overlapping special case, not stronger coverage of \(d=3\) or \(d\ge5\). The theorem is accepted for the genuinely broader different-polar family, not for its already-covered \(d=4\) corollary.

value.rationale: The exact all-dimensional closed form yields the strict three-dimensional lower bound \(14\), contradicting a clearly documented \(12\) conjecture for quantitative illumination. A general structural efficiency lemma simultaneously explains why gauge cost differs from ordinary illumination number. The classification is natural and sharp; there is no claim to a general upper bound.
